chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban and Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, who both said: Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said:

When you stand for salat (prayer), then say: O Allah, I present Muhammad before You ahead of my need, and I turn by him toward You; so make me, by him, distinguished in Your sight in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near. Make my salat accepted, my sin forgiven, and my supplication through him answered. Indeed, You are the All-Forgiving, the All-Merciful.

key_terms.حَاجَتِي: my need, the request or concern presented before Allah
key_terms.دُعَائِي: my supplication, asked to be answered
key_terms.ذَنْبِي: my sin, for which forgiveness is sought
key_terms.صَلَاتِي: my salat (prayer), for which acceptance is requested
key_terms.مُحَمَّدًا: Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, through whom one seeks approach to Allah
key_terms.وَجِيهًا: distinguished and honored in rank before Allah
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act of worship before which this supplication is recited
key_terms.ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ: those brought near, meaning those granted nearness to Allah

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited when standing for salat (prayer) according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a supplication to be recited when standing for salat (prayer), seeking nearness to Allah through Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It asks for acceptance of prayer, forgiveness of sins, and an answered du'a, while affirming Allah as the All-Forgiving and All-Merciful.
